exposure_anchors.1: Negligible: no public-sector touchpoints, no agents / intermediaries, no permitting or licensing, jurisdictions with low corruption perception.
exposure_anchors.2: Limited: occasional public-sector interface (filings, certifications), no agents.
exposure_anchors.3: Moderate: regular permitting / inspection / licensing interface; some use of intermediaries.
exposure_anchors.4: High: significant public-sector interface (procurement, infrastructure); agents in higher-corruption jurisdictions.
exposure_anchors.5: Severe: defence / extractives / large infrastructure; multiple agents in CPI > 50 jurisdictions; politically-connected counterparties.

threat_credibility_anchors.1: No documented ABC enforcement in this sector / region.
threat_credibility_anchors.3: Active enforcement in the sector / region.
threat_credibility_anchors.4: Active and adapted: corruption schemes documented in adjacent firms.
threat_credibility_anchors.5: Active and targeted: prior ABC enforcement contact or sector listed as enforcement priority.

vulnerability_anchors.1: Adequate Procedures (UKBA s.7) demonstrably in place + audited.
vulnerability_anchors.2: Adequate Procedures broadly in place with minor gaps.
vulnerability_anchors.3: Programme partial: policy + training present, agent DD inconsistent, register weak.
vulnerability_anchors.4: Programme weak: multiple controls absent or untested.
vulnerability_anchors.5: No ABC programme; reliance on individual judgement.
